reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the finding correctly carries no redline and no counterparty comment — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong has been proposed.

The cited text supports the compliance call on the rule's material terms: the exculpation in Section 6.2(a) (p0283, Servicer/Marketing Agent) is word-for-word mirrored for the Depositor in Section 5.2(a) (p0243), so the limitation is mutual and the walk-away scenario (our side uncapped while the counterparty is capped) does not arise.

No monetary cap exists on the counterparty (no 'aggregate liability'/'shall not exceed' language), and the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's indemnities at p0291-p0292 are uncapped with no super-cap ceiling; this is more favourable to us than the preferred 12-months'-fees / USD 1,000,000 construct, and the rule expressly warns against caps measured on a small fee base (here a monthly percentage of principal). Proposing a fees cap would be adverse to our own party and would breach the 'do not flag a clause that benefits our party' instruction.

The fallback's minimum carve-out set (indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) sits outside any limitation, and 'bad faith' substantially covers fraud; Section 9.6 limited recourse (p0378) further caps our own exposure to the Depositor Transferred Property.

The failed deterministic check ('cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor') is expected and not probative here — the absence of a fee-based cap is the very reason the clause exceeds the playbook position rather than falling short of it.

Correctly handled residual gaps as noted-not-flagged: no express uncapped carve-out for confidentiality, data protection/security or IP infringement, and no mutual consequential-damages exclusion — minor sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not defeat the fallback. Worth recording internally that the exculpation limits counterparty liability to wilful misconduct/bad faith/gross negligence (i.e. no liability for ordinary negligent breach), but it is mutual and market-standard for a securitization transfer and servicing agreement.
